players.product: proprietary single-molecule tracking (SMT) platform with AI/ML-guided drug discovery

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Roger Perlmutter on the super-resolution microscopy platform, which he calls over the long term the most important source of value for the company (though a minority of expense, since clinical trial expenses are significant for a late-stage company): Eikon's entirely proprietary instruments evaluate millions of cells per day and typically 10 to 100,000 proteins per cell, imaging usually at about 100 frames per second (frame rates higher than 1,000 frames per second are possible) with roughly 10-millisecond time resolution and roughly 10 to 30 nanometer spatial resolution. When the instruments are all running full tilt, which they often are, Eikon in Milpitas, California produces on the order of a petabyte of data a day; he calls it one of the largest data producers in the world. Screening assays can screen 1 million compounds or so in roughly 6 weeks, and the Werner helicase inhibitor went from the initial lead to a development candidate in about 16 months. The novel androgen receptor antagonist, originally planned for an IND filing in 2027, will now have its IND filed before the end of this year because the analysis was done so fast. CEO: the tools will let Eikon bring forward important new molecules much more rapidly.
quarterly_data.figure: millions of cells per day; 10 to 100,000 proteins per cell; about 100 frames per second; roughly 10-millisecond time resolution; 10 to 30 nanometer spatial resolution; on the order of a petabyte of data a day; 1 million compounds in roughly 6 weeks; lead to development candidate in about 16 months; AR antagonist IND moved from 2027 to before the end of this year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on therapeutic areas beyond oncology: because the platform can visualize living neurons, Eikon has expanded into neurodegeneration, studying misfolded proteins in living neurons with the aim of identifying components involved in the correct folding or refolding of toxic misfolded proteins; it has also been active in inflammatory disease, where he says there are good targets, and he is open to discovery work addressing cardiovascular disease.

CEO on the selective PARP1 inhibitors: Eikon searched for the most selective PARP1 inhibitors and found a set of molecules at a small company called IMPACT in China, run by Dr. Tsai; it filed the INDs and advanced two of them. The non-brain-penetrant EIK-1003, the most advanced, is about 650-fold selective for PARP1 over PARP2 and has been used to treat more than 250 patients, showing less myelosuppression than dual PARP1/PARP2 inhibitors; the brain-penetrant EIK-1004 is about 800-fold selective at the enzymatic level, has been studied in around 75 patients and has completed multiple ascending dose studies, which he says support the hypothesis that selective PARP1 inhibition spares the hematopoietic system. CEO: to his knowledge combining a PARP inhibitor with full-dose paclitaxel had never been possible before (he says they tried very hard with LYNPARZA and could not); this could take PARP inhibitors beyond maintenance into second-line and possibly first-line treatment (for first-line with platinum 'We have no data there'); he calls Eikon's PARP inhibitors 'certainly the most advanced, highly selective PARP1 inhibitors right now in clinical development'.
quarterly_data.figure: about 650-fold (EIK-1003) and about 800-fold (EIK-1004) selectivity for PARP1 over PARP2; more than 250 patients treated with EIK-1003; around 75 patients studied on EIK-1004
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: source of the PARP1 inhibitor molecules

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the PARP1 development plan: Eikon is in the midst of a detailed analysis of possible indications (lines of therapy, monotherapy, maintenance and combinations) and has distilled them down to 12 studies, on a path to a small set of registration-enabling studies meant to bring EIK-1003 and EIK-1004 ultimately to the marketplace; it will announce the registration-enabling studies when designed, possibly not at ESMO, because it first wants discussions with regulatory agencies. At ESMO the key EIK-1003 update is the first abiraterone combination data in prostate cancer; CEO: the rate of blood transfusion with novel hormonal agents plus PARP inhibitors is on the order of 50%, so showing the expected responses with less hematologic toxicity would be very important for Eikon. For EIK-1004 he is very comfortable with the safety profile so far; breast cancer patients at high risk of intracranial malignancy are a good place to go with it, and the studies are enrolling patients at risk for active brain metastases.
quarterly_data.figure: 12 candidate studies distilled; blood transfusion rate on the order of 50% with novel hormonal agents plus PARP inhibitors (CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the EIK-1001 seamless Phase II/III programs (event driven, overseen by an independent data monitoring committee, company blinded internally): the first interim analysis of the melanoma study collapsed the dose from two doses to one, so it is now a two-arm study instead of a three-arm study. The second interim analysis, the first indication of efficacy, on which the committee recommends expanding further into Phase III or pausing to evaluate the Phase II data, comes sometime during the first half of 2027, and Eikon will announce the outcome within days of knowing. Enrollment rates are so high that he expects to complete melanoma enrollment and, depending on event rate, complete the melanoma study first; the non-small cell lung cancer study (EIK-1001 with KEYTRUDA and chemotherapy versus standard of care alone, squamous and non-squamous), which is just spooling up, is probably going to enroll even faster and catch up, by design, with Eikon hoping for results for both in a similar timeframe. The Phase II NSCLC update at ESMO will include patients who have been on study for 2 years.
quarterly_data.figure: melanoma study now two-arm (from three-arm); second interim analysis sometime during the first half of 2027; Phase II patients on study for 2 years

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Freddy Bowie: Eikon had $531.2 million of cash at the half-year and is burning roughly $75 million of cash every quarter supporting its studies, two-thirds of it directed to clinical work; year over year the research and engineering spend has gone down while the company has become more effective at developing candidates headed to the clinic.
quarterly_data.figure: cash burn roughly $75 million per quarter; two-thirds to clinical work
